### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s).

**57** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d4d8a87d3323888617106b4e4685aa3ed61fb760` — the merge of head `749c7a2ca3fb18acbfa87c9e6b22e576824c4563` into base `0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d4d8a87d3323888617106b4e4685aa3ed61fb760 && git checkout d4d8a87d3323888617106b4e4685aa3ed61fb760
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80 749c7a2ca3fb18acbfa87c9e6b22e576824c4563 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80 && git merge --no-ff 749c7a2ca3fb18acbfa87c9e6b22e576824c4563

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0241df4d6b2dc9611b382c9269665e9493101e80` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fb0d4b052dde4dfccfc8ad85dd11fe4af3af6f52`
Local-runs: none
Scope: plugin-auth (`auth-manager.ts`, `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`, `auth-manager-after-hook.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `auth-route-ledger.ts`, `oauth-authorize-refusal.ts`, `oauth-callback-refusal-reason.ts`, `oauth-client-name.ts`), Console sign-in page and its two helpers, three i18n keys in eleven packs, tests, `.changeset/34168-authorize-gate-refusal-reason.md`

### ① Derived judgments

- The face owed is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone: no `packages/spec/src/**` file, no governed path (`check-governed-merges --pr 34265`: 0 of 27 paths governed, 1291 lines), no narrowing line.
- The gate seam widens its answer type only. An object refuses exactly when it says `allowed: false`; every other answer keeps the truthiness it was read with, so the admitted set is unchanged (pinned, with a boolean CONTROL whose three refusal replies are byte-identical to the merge base).
- Every host value is validated before it is served: a reason outside the closed shape is dropped and the refusal stands; a sentence that fails the length, markup or (on the redirect) RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 character rules is replaced by the fixed sentence. The page escapes it.
- The callback carry only re-attaches a reason the refusal itself sent, on the platform identity provider's callback, under `access_denied` on both sides, and keeps the rest of the location byte for byte. Each condition has a red ablation in the body.
- The new public read answers one field, and only for the client its signed request names; every other case answers one identical 404. The session is never read. It is ledgered `public` and the mount-ledger gate passes.
- Each changeset sentence was checked against the diff: the refusal object, the envelope `reason`, the redirect parameter, the escaped page sentence, the validation rules, the callback carry, the two Console sentences, the client-name route, the unchanged boolean path, and the upgrade note.

### ② Semver level

patch for plugin-auth, console and i18n: an optional field, an optional redirect parameter, one read route and three keys are added; nothing an older caller sends or reads moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Access boundary: who is admitted does not change. The new unauthenticated read discloses only a client's display name, only to a holder of a request this server signed for that client.
- No served→refused change, so no `!`, BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker owed.
- Open to the seat: the ADR-0138 D2 record of the new unauthenticated route and its ADR-0121 D6 posture (`docs/adr/**` is outside this card's surface).
- Pins in card-named files; the round-2 ablations each go red on exactly one pin.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `749c7a2ca3fb18acbfa87c9e6b22e576824c4563`
Local-runs: none

The face is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone. The diff touches no published schema and no governed path (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth`, `ui/apps/console`, `ui/packages/i18n`), and it declares no narrowing. Inputs: card #34168, the PR body and changeset, the net diff against merge base `babda9d3`, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The gate's answer widens, and admission does not move: right.** `oidcAuthorizeGate` may answer `{ allowed: false, reason, message }` in place of `false`. An object refuses only on `allowed === false`. A boolean, and any other object, keeps the truthiness the gate was always read with, so nobody is admitted or refused differently. A boolean answer is byte-identical on all three doors, and the CONTROL pins say so.
- **Host text is never trusted as markup or as a URL part: right.** `reason` must match `[a-z_]{1,40}`; otherwise it is dropped and the refusal stands. A `message` longer than 300 characters, or one holding a control character or an angle bracket, is replaced by the fixed sentence. On the redirect it must also fit the RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 `error_description` charset. The page HTML-escapes it. The vendor-prefixed `objectstack_error_reason` follows RFC 6749 §8.2.
- **The callback carries one validated reason only: right.** The platform-IdP callback keeps a valid `objectstack_error_reason` on its redirect to the Console sign-in page only under `access_denied` on both sides, with exactly one reason of the validated shape. The rest of the location is kept byte for byte. The Console maps `not_member` and `invitation_pending` to its own sentences in all eleven packs; anything else keeps the existing `access_denied` sentence.
- **The new signed-out route is closed and bounded: right.** `GET /oauth2/client-name` answers a name only for the client its signed request names. Every other state gets one uniform `404`, a parameter outside the closed set gets `400`, and every answer is `no-store`. The route is ledgered `public`. At this head it is rate-limited per established client address, as ADR-0121 D6 asks of a door that admits an anonymous caller: 10 reads per 60 s, counted before anything is parsed or read, answering `429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After`. That is line for line the signed-out invitation preview's window, with its own counter subject, wired in the same unconditional `init()` block.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author writes changes. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds: a host gains an answer shape and a client gains optional keys and one route; nothing accepted before is refused. This is not a protocol change, so `patch` is right on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n`, the three packages moved. `Check Changeset` is green. No migration entry or ADR-0087 disposition is owed, and no `Skills-docs:` line is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Version skew is the one hazard, and the changeset states it.** An older plugin-auth reads any object as an admission, so a host must not return the refusal object before it runs this release. The upgrade note says so.
- **Owed outside this diff: an ADR note for the new unauthenticated door.** The PR's acceptance notes say ADR-0138 D2 asks for one and leave it to the seat, because `docs/adr/**` is outside the card's surface. It needs a carrier. It does not block this PR.
- The callback carry covers the `GET` callback only. A `form_post` provider would lose the reason on the vendor's re-issued `GET`. The platform IdP answers by query redirect, so no caller reaches that path today.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A1-34168`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `749c7a2ca3fb18acbfa87c9e6b22e576824c4563`
Reviewer: review-a (S1) · 2026-11-16T07:36Z
Implemented-by: S1 area dev (`claude/area-A1-34168`)
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM`
Diff base: `babda9d3` (merge base with `origin/main`); 27 files, +1357/−29. I read the diff up to `fb0d4b05` before the rate-limit round; this read covers that whole diff plus the round-3 delta (`1a07deec`, `749c7a2c`).

### What holds

- **Items 1 and 2: the gate's refusal can say why, without moving admission.** `gateAnswerRefuses` refuses an object only on `allowed === false` and keeps truthiness for every other answer. `refusalDetailOf` validates the reason (`^[a-z_]{1,40}$`) and the sentence (at most 300 characters, no control characters or angle brackets, and on the redirect the RFC 6749 `error_description` charset), and falls back to the fixed sentence otherwise. The page escapes it. The boolean CONTROL pins hold the envelope, the redirect parameter order and the page bytes equal to the merge base's.
- **Item 3: the callback carry is narrow.** It is a `GET` of the platform identity provider's callback, with `error=access_denied` on both the request and the redirect, exactly one reason of the validated shape, and no reason already present. The location is otherwise kept byte for byte. Each condition has its own ablation, and each ablation reds exactly its pin. The Console reads the reason only under `access_denied`, and all eleven packs carry real translations (zh-Hant generated).
- **Item 4: the application-name route.** The signature is verified by the provider's own `verifyOAuthQueryParams`. The URL `client_id` must equal the single signed one. The client is read under system context for `name` and `disabled` only. Every failure gets one `404`, the parameter set is closed, and every answer is `no-store`. The session is never read. The Console asks once, renders the name as text through i18n, and keeps the host line on any other answer.
- **Round 3: the seat's rate-limit ruling is met.** `answerOAuthClientName` counts the per-address fixed window (10 per 60 s) before parsing, in the counter store the signed-out invitation preview uses, under its own subject. It answers `429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After` and `no-store`. The counters are wired in the same unconditional `init()` block as the preview's, and the route fails closed (`500`) if they were never wired. The new pin covers the window, the 429 and a second address that still answers. Removing the limit reds it ("expected 200 to be 429").

### Must

None.

### Should

None for this PR. One carrier is owed outside the diff: the ADR-0138 D2 note recording the new unauthenticated door, which the PR leaves to the seat because `docs/adr/**` is outside the card. It is in the contract record's boundary flags.

### Nits

1. `useHandoffClientName` fetches with `credentials: 'include'`, though the route never reads the session. `'omit'` would state that intent.
2. Callers whose address the server could not establish share one `unestablished` bucket, so behind a misconfigured proxy they can exhaust each other's window. That is the invitation preview's existing posture, and the page degrades to the host line, so the impact is cosmetic.
3. The callback carry does not survive a `form_post` provider (stated in the PR). No caller reaches that path today.

### Gates

70 check runs at this head (latest run of each): every one is success or skipped, none failed or pending. This includes Test Core 1–8/8, Test UI 1–16/16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Check Changeset. The PR body records the plugin-auth suite (5668 passed) and typecheck at this head, and `merge-tree` against `origin/main` is clean.

The TIER_DEFAULT contract record for the widening is comment 6910359938 (PASS), written in the same pass.
